source_policy.primary_search_strategy: scholarly/peer-reviewed literature prioritized; publisher/DOI records used for bibliographic verification
source_policy.permitted_use: citation metadata, DOI/URL, bibliographic facts, and project-authored evidence summaries only
source_policy.rights_note: Open-access or Creative Commons indicators are recorded only as candidate metadata. No source is rights-approved or content-ingestion-approved by this review.

duplicate_review.note: Concepts intentionally recur across modules only where instructional context differs (for example evidence correlation, vehicle-specific applicability, and verification). No item is redundant enough to remove in this batch.

safety_review.note: Automated/content review found no prohibited universal service values. Human technical/safety sign-off is still required.

questions.claim_review: Direct battery measurements should be distinguished from calculated/estimated battery states.
questions.source_applicability_notes: The review explicitly distinguishes directly measured voltage/current/temperature from estimated battery states such as SOC/SOH.

questions.claim_review: Battery conclusions should correlate multiple compatible observations rather than rely on one isolated data point.
questions.source_applicability_notes: The literature supports multi-parameter BMS monitoring and multi-source fault diagnosis; wording remains project-authored diagnostic pedagogy.

questions.claim_review: SOC is an estimated/calculated state rather than a direct physical measurement of stored energy.
questions.source_applicability_notes: Directly supported by the battery state-estimation review.

questions.claim_review: Battery access/isolation should follow applicable vehicle-specific procedures and verified electrical state.
questions.hold_reason: Needs an authoritative vehicle-service or high-voltage service-safety source that directly supports service-procedure dependence; general academic architecture sources are not sufficient for service authorization.

questions.claim_review: Comparing commanded state with measured response helps identify divergence between control intent and actual operation.
questions.source_applicability_notes: General diagnostic/fault-monitoring literature supports command/measurement comparison and multi-sensor diagnosis; exact phrasing is project-authored.

questions.claim_review: An inverter/converter-related fault indication can involve interacting supply, control, communication, thermal, machine, or internal-protection factors.
questions.source_applicability_notes: Sources support interacting EV power-electronic/control subsystems and fault-diagnosis complexity; question deliberately avoids component-failure inference.

questions.claim_review: Regenerative operation converts mechanical/electrical-machine energy back to electrical energy under permitted conditions.
questions.source_applicability_notes: The review describes reversed inverter energy flow during regenerative operation.

questions.claim_review: Actual vehicle power-electronics architecture should be established before applying topology-specific interpretations.
questions.source_applicability_notes: Both reviews document multiple converter, machine, and charging architectures rather than a single universal topology.

questions.claim_review: Charging diagnosis benefits from separating infrastructure, interface, vehicle conversion/control, battery, and thermal boundaries.
questions.source_applicability_notes: The charging review distinguishes EVSE/infrastructure, onboard/offboard conversion, vehicle/battery interfaces, control, and standards.

questions.claim_review: A will-not-charge symptom alone does not identify a failed component because charging depends on multiple coordinated conditions.
questions.source_applicability_notes: Charging architecture and control are multi-stage and topology-dependent; symptom-to-component inference is not justified from architecture alone.

questions.claim_review: Connection recognition/readiness-state evidence should be established before escalating to more invasive charging diagnosis.
questions.source_applicability_notes: The review supports staged charging architecture/control and communication dependencies; the nonintrusive-first ordering is project-authored pedagogy requiring human technical review.

questions.claim_review: Temperature interpretation requires operating context, plausibility, thermal control response, trends, and applicable limits.
questions.source_applicability_notes: The review documents subsystem thermal demands that vary with driving conditions and ambient temperature.

questions.claim_review: Reduced performance associated with temperature may reflect several thermal/control causes and should be correlated before naming a failed component.
questions.source_applicability_notes: Integrated thermal systems and fault-diagnosis literature support multi-factor interpretation rather than single-clue replacement.

questions.claim_review: Universal thermal thresholds are inappropriate because architectures, subsystem requirements, and operating conditions differ.
questions.source_applicability_notes: The review explicitly describes different thermal loads and strategies across batteries, motors, electronics, cabins, ambient and driving conditions.

questions.claim_review: Low-voltage power supports EV auxiliary/control loads and can affect vehicle readiness even when the traction battery is charged.
questions.source_applicability_notes: The IEEE review strongly supports HV-to-LV supply and 12 V/auxiliary loads; the industry source corroborates control-module/contactors/wake-up context. Stronger scholarly support for wake-up/contactors would improve this item.

questions.claim_review: Simultaneous module unavailability can arise from a shared power, ground, wake-up, network, or timing dependency.
questions.hold_reason: Needs an authoritative automotive network/electrical diagnostic source directly addressing common-cause/shared-dependency diagnosis; current source is too general.

questions.claim_review: A readiness-first strategy should collect foundational nonintrusive evidence before higher-risk testing.
questions.hold_reason: This is a defensible instructional strategy but the current scholarly source does not directly establish the diagnostic ordering or safety rationale. Hold for technical reviewer plus service-diagnostics evidence.

questions.claim_review: The project-authored Request → Measure → Compare → Correlate → Verify model defines Compare as comparing observations with applicable authoritative information and expected context.
questions.hold_reason: The five-stage model is project-authored. External literature supports fault diagnosis and multi-source comparison generally, but not this exact framework. Requires internal curriculum provenance plus human technical validation rather than pretending an external source originated the model.

questions.claim_review: Competing hypotheses and discriminating evidence reduce premature single-cause conclusions.
questions.hold_reason: Current EV fault-diagnosis reviews support multi-source/model-based diagnosis but do not directly establish the specific competing-hypothesis pedagogy. Hold for a stronger diagnostic-method source or explicit technical reviewer approval.

questions.claim_review: Post-repair verification should confirm the original concern and relevant system behavior rather than rely only on clearing fault codes.
questions.hold_reason: Needs authoritative service-diagnostics evidence explicitly supporting post-repair verification; current review supports diagnosis/monitoring but not the code-clearing comparison.
